The paper trains a novel semi-supervised multi-task learning model on GP EHR data to predict eGFR trends, using both labeled and abundant unlabeled patients. No specific model architecture or algorithm is named in the abstract, so model_type and model_family are left empty.

The paper trains a well-established kernel-based regression model on known compound-kinase binding affinities to predict unmeasured drug-target interactions, then validates 100 predictions experimentally. The paper trains 21 CNN architectures (best: DenseNet169) and CNN ensembles on the COVIDx8B chest X-ray dataset for supervised COVID-19 classification. The domain is AI-based medical image diagnosis, best captured by Medicine/Imaging/Medical imaging.

The paper trains a supervised deep learning model (8CSL: 8-layer CNN with shortcut connections plus an LSTM layer) on ECG recordings for atrial fibrillation classification, evaluated on the CinC 2017 dataset. The study validates and compares two pre-built segmentation algorithms from the Lesion Segmentation Toolbox against visual and manual ratings, tuning only their initial probability thresholds without training any model. The paper trains a deep learning model end-to-end on μCT images of mouse bones to predict skeletal age (supervised classification/regression of time points), but names no specific architecture, so only the deep learning family is tagged. The paper trains support vector machines on recurrence-based combustion noise features from pressure sensor data to predict thermoacoustic instabilities, a supervised task. The application domain is combustion/rocket physics with applied machine learning; no deeper domain terms fit.

The paper trains DNN, graph convolutional, random forest and multivariate logistic regression classifiers/regressors on chemical featurizations to predict androgen receptor binding, a cheminformatics/toxicology (QSAR-style) task. The paper trains a similarity learning method on students' triplet-comparison responses (supervised, trained in this study) to detect the visual features driving perceptual judgments of chemistry representations such as Lewis structures. The paper reports a custom-built reinforcement learning system, Eva, trained and deployed on real-time traveler data to allocate COVID-19 border testing. The paper applies synchronous fluorescence spectroscopy with PCA, PCA-Gaussian mixture model clustering and self-organising maps to authenticate COVID-19 vaccines, an analytical-chemistry/vaccinology task. The paper trains two models (a response-predicting model and a generative inverse-design model) that assist a genetic algorithm used as the paper's own search/optimization method, so both are trained in this study in a supervised manner. The paper trains an iterative deep neural network on experimental laser drilling data to predict microchannel structures and optimize processing parameters. The paper trains a neuroimaging-based multivariable regression model on cohort MRI-derived features to predict calendar age (brain-age gap), a supervised regression task with no named deep or ensemble architecture. The paper trains a maximum entropy (MaxEnt) ecological niche model on environmental and socioeconomic variables to map scrub typhus suitability (AUC 0.864), a supervised classical ML approach; the negative binomial regression is used only to test risk-factor associations, so it is excluded as a model type. The domain is disease distribution/epidemiology of a vector-borne disease, hence Medicine with Public health and epidemiology and Parasitology.

The study characterizes barley seed microbial communities across continents and trains a machine learning classifier to trace geographic origin (95% accuracy), implying supervised learning, but no specific algorithm is named so model_type/family stay empty. Domains center on microbiology/metagenomics of seed-associated communities with an agricultural quarantine application.

The paper trains a cross-domain transfer learning radiomics model (supervised classification of lung granulomatous nodules vs adenocarcinoma) using adaptive transfer learning, a named family, but the abstract names no specific underlying algorithm or architecture, so model_type is left empty; the Wasserstein distance is a domain-similarity metric, not a model.

RNAmigos2 trains a graph neural network on RNA binding-pocket graphs with RNA-centric self-supervised pretraining plus supervised ranking, so it is trained in this study under supervised and self-supervised paradigms with deep learning and representation-learning families. The domain is computational drug discovery for RNA targets screened against small-molecule libraries.

The paper trains its own PPINet network (self-attention based, hence deep learning) on labelled PPI-site data, so it is supervised training, and combines base models trained on different features via stacking, an ensemble learning technique. The subject is sequence-based prediction of protein-protein interaction sites, placing it in computational biology/bioinformatics with protein interaction and protein site feature domains.

The paper trains a supervised risk-identification classifier on annotated patient narratives (PsyRisk/PsyTAR corpora) to predict antidepressant discontinuation, a psychiatry/pharmacovigilance application built on NLP-derived text data. The abstract names no specific algorithm or model architecture, only 'machine learning-driven', so model_type and model_family remain empty.

The paper trains a machine-learning-derived LLPSI signature on TCGA/GEO data for supervised survival/prognosis prediction, but the abstract names no specific algorithm ('machine learning method'), so model_type and model_family stay empty; the nomogram ('column line figure') is a statistical visualization tool, not an ML model. The subject is HCC prognosis and immunotherapy response prediction using a gene-signature biomarker.

The paper trains multiclass SVM classifiers (RBF, polynomial, linear kernels) on autofluorescence spectral features of standard proteins, a supervised classical-ML approach; mRMR is feature selection and is therefore not tagged as a model type. The subject domain is protein identification based on spectral properties, fitting analytical-chemistry/protein analysis.

The study trains a lasso feature-selection step and a multivariate logistic regression prediction model on its own cohort of hospitalized adolescents with depression. The subject is clinical psychiatry (suicide risk in adolescent depression), so Medicine/Psychiatry apply.

The paper fits PCA on strain sensor data (with FEA-simulated damage cases) to detect and localize structural damage, an unsupervised dimensional-reduction approach; 'Machine Learning' is named only generically, so no further model types are tagged. The subject is structural/aircraft health monitoring, which falls outside the biomedical domain vocabularies, so no domain terms apply.

The study trains an Iterative Dichotomiser 3 decision tree (and references support vector machine mapping) on multispectral satellite bands to classify burn extent and biomass consumption, a supervised classification task in ecology/remote sensing of wildland fire. No deep learning, generative, or agentic methods are involved.

The study trains supervised ML models on labeled patient data (CD vs CRC); polynomial regression was selected as optimal after comparison with eight algorithms including LSTM, which the authors themselves trained. The domain is differential diagnosis of colorectal cancer vs Crohn's disease using genetic/epigenetic fecal biomarkers.

The paper developed and trained the Powerscribe Smart Impression NLP algorithm on 9.8 million radiology reports to generate impression sections from dictated findings, a supervised text-to-impression generation task. Statistical analyses (Pearson correlation, paired t-tests, AUC) were evaluation methods, not the paper's models.

The paper applies ab initio and machine learning potential molecular dynamics with metadynamics to study Fe-doped MgO carbonation for CO2 capture; the ML potential is trained (typically on ab initio reference data) to run the simulations, and the domain is materials/chemistry-focused with computational chemistry and molecular dynamics as central tiers.

The paper trains CatBoost regression models (including five hybrid variants) on mining land subsidence data, with the metaheuristic optimizers (ALO, BES, BSA, HHO, SSA) serving only as hyperparameter tuners rather than standalone models, and Shapley values used purely for explanation. The subject is mining-environmental prediction, which falls under Environmental science in tier 2 but has no matching biomedical tier 1 or tier 3 term.

The study applies the pretrained AlphaFold-Multimer model as-is to screen plant-pathogen protein pairs for interactions, with no training or fine-tuning reported. Domains reflect plant-pathogen molecular interaction research and protein structure/interaction prediction.

model_type: ["continuous attractor network", "Hebbian learning", "dopamine-modulated three-factor rule (reinforcement learning)"]
rationale: The paper builds and trains a neurocomputational model of hippocampal replay and navigation, using Hebbian (unsupervised) learning of place-cell synapses and a dopamine-modulated three-factor (reinforcement) rule for place-reward associations in striatal neurons. The core architecture is a continuous attractor neural network, a shallow neural network, validated in the MuJoCo physics simulator.

The paper trains an Extra Trees Classifier on retrospective clinical data to predict gastrointestinal bleeding risk in spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage patients, a supervised task in neurology/critical care. Boruta, Information-Gain, Spearman correlation and SHAP are feature-selection/interpretability methods, not model types.

The study trains predictive models (Prophet, LightGBM, XGBoost) on year-long sensor data of grapevine growth, a supervised regression/forecasting task in plant/agricultural science. LightGBM and XGBoost are gradient-boosting ensembles within classical machine learning; Prophet is a time-series forecasting model tagged verbatim.

The study trains simple ML classifiers, with XGBoost named as the best-performing one, on manually measured retinal features for MS vs healthy control classification, and applies a previously proposed deep learning segmentation algorithm as-is with pre/post-processing. Domains reflect the ophthalmic imaging application (SLO retinal images) in the neurological disease multiple sclerosis.

The paper trains DNA shape-based models of mutation rates on human genome data, an evidently supervised predictive/regression task, but the abstract names no specific ML algorithm or model family, so model_type and model_family are left empty. The subject domain is human genome mutation-rate variation, tagged under genetics/genomics with DNA mutation and genetic variation as tier-3 topics.

The paper trains an autoencoder for unsupervised embedding of paired methylation-expression features, then trains ANN and CNN classifiers on the latent space (supervised) for glioma subtyping. Cox regression and GSEA are association/feature-selection analyses, not the paper's predictive models.

The paper trains a novel stochastic reinforcement learning framework on financial data, using a Gaussian-mixture-parameterized stochastic policy with a quantile-based distributional critic and a risk-aware reward. Deterministic and stochastic RL benchmarks are comparators, so only the proposed policy-gradient-based framework is tagged; no biomedical domain applies beyond computer science/applied mathematics.

The paper trains a gradient boosting regression tree on a curated enzyme-variant dataset to guide stereodivergent directed evolution of carboxylesterase AcEst1, a supervised regression task. The domain is enzyme/biocatalyst engineering (biocatalysis chemistry) supported by machine learning; molecular dynamics and QM/MM are simulations, not ML models, and are excluded from model_type.

The paper trains a population-split-based supervised ML risk model for VTE, benchmarked against SVM, random forest, GBDT, logistic regression and XGBoost, so classical ML and ensemble families apply. The domain is clinical risk prediction in medicine with an ML method focus; no tier-3 term is central.

The paper trains a semantic-encoding NLP knowledge-mining model on CMF Clearinghouse data to predict Crash Modification Factors from unstructured countermeasure descriptions, a supervised text-encoding regression task in road-safety (traffic injury prevention) research. No specific model architecture or algorithm is named in the abstract, so no model_type is tagged beyond the NLP family.

The study applies pretrained LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o) via prompting and also fine-tunes smaller LLMs on labelled cardiac reports, a supervised classification task. Domains reflect the cardiology report-extraction application and clinical informatics; no tier3 term is clearly central since only report text (not imaging data) is analysed.

The paper applies a 3D U-Net for hepatic vessel segmentation on gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI to quantify vessel-to-volume ratios across chronic liver disease stages, an imaging-based hepatology study. The abstract does not describe training or fine-tuning of the U-Net, so it is treated as applied as-is, and no learning paradigm is claimed.

The paper trains a novel stacked fusion network (ResGCN plus CNNs feeding AdaBoostRF) for supervised survival prediction on multi-omics data, so deep learning, classical ML, and ensemble families all apply. t-SNE is used only as a validation/visualization step and Kaplan-Meier is a statistical survival analysis, so neither is listed as a model type.

The paper trains a hybrid XGBoost+MLP stacking ensemble on clinical data for supervised PCOS prediction, with Chi-Square/RFE feature selection (not a model type) and SHAP/LIME excluded as explainability methods. Domain is endocrine disease prediction (PCOS) using machine learning.

The paper is a cell-biology imaging method development (LaBeRling) for labeling ER-membrane contact sites, evaluated by light microscopy and a deep-learning volume electron microscopy approach. The deep-learning analysis is applied as-is with no named architecture or training described, so only the deep learning family and no specific model type are tagged.

model_type: ["neural network", "genetic algorithm", "naive Bayes", "random forest", "decision tree", "support vector machine"]

All models are trained/supervised on the Diabetes 130-US hospital dataset, and the domain is ML applied to medical record classification.

The paper applies PLS-DA on breath mass spectrometry data to discriminate healthy volunteers, chronic hepatitis B, and liver failure patients, so the model is trained in-study in a supervised, classical-ML paradigm. The subject is breath metabolomics and biomarker/metabolic-pathway discovery for liver disease.

The paper trains a Kolmogorov-Arnold network (SepOKAN) and a physics-constrained variant (SPIKAN) to model ultra-wideband optical fiber channels, fitting physical equations and validating on real WDM link data (supervised training). MLP is only a comparator, so it is not tagged.

A precision-agriculture paper developing a machine learning algorithm that learns site-specific management through iterative on-farm experiments (closed-loop, query-driven experiment learning), so the domain is agricultural science with machine learning, and the model is trained on the farm-experiment data. The abstract names no specific algorithm or architecture, so model_type is left empty; the closed-loop learning from on-farm experiments is tagged as active learning, and the learning is supervised from experimental outcomes.

The paper trains a supervised random forest classifier on literature-derived plasma essential amino acid data to assign individual dairy cows to previously identified EAA clusters, evaluating it with leave-one-trial-out cross-validation. The subject domain is dairy cow nutrition and performance, best captured under agricultural/animal science.

The authors train a hybrid CNN + Vision Transformer model on LDCT images plus clinical data for mediastinal tumour diagnosis, and also train random forest and logistic regression radiomics baselines for comparison. All models are supervised; the domain is oncological/imaging medicine.

The paper trains a cross-modality image generation model (the standard GAN-based synthesis approach, implied by paired-image generation, feature exchange and latent-space sampling) for RGB-IR person re-identification, with unsupervised alignment across unpaired modalities plus supervised identity feature learning. Domains reflect a computer-vision/machine-learning study with no biomedical subject matter.

The paper trains a random forest model to rank cold-responsive candidate genes from RNA-seq data (supervised, OOB evaluation), and applies AlphaFold3 as-is for structural prediction of candidates. The subject is alfalfa transcriptomics and transcription factor genomics.

The paper trains four deep learning image classifiers (DenseNet121, VGG-16, ResNet50, vision transformer) with 5-fold cross-validation on labelled pediatric VCE images, i.e., supervised training of models in this study. Domain focus is pediatric gastroenterology with endoscopic (medical) imaging; Grad-CAM is explainability and excluded from model_type.

The paper trains XGBoost, random forest, and cross-validated linear regression on SEER-Medicare data to predict health care expenditures, a supervised regression task; SHAP is an interpretability method and is not tagged as a model type. The domain is health-services/cost research in older Hodgkin lymphoma survivors, best captured by Medicine, Oncology, and Public health and epidemiology.

The paper trains a supervised omics-based binary classification pipeline with feature selection and synthetic-data augmentation, but the abstract names no specific algorithm, architecture, or tool, so model_type and model_family remain empty per the evidence rules. The subject is machine-learning analysis of omics data for clinical diagnostics.

The paper retrospectively clusters standardized clinical/biochemical variables of AKI patients with k-means to derive phenotypes linked to major adverse kidney events. This is an unsupervised classical ML application on nephrology cohort data, with no supervised, deep, or prompted components.

The paper applies unsupervised k-means clustering with stability-based validation to structural MRI-derived features of MDD patients, then trains a support vector machine to predict cluster labels. Domains reflect the psychiatric clinical focus and the structural neuroimaging (MRI) data modality.

The paper trains a fully-convolutional neural network on DNS data of a turbulent boundary layer and fine-tunes it on experimental water-tunnel measurements, an explicit transfer-learning setup for supervised velocity-field prediction. The subject is fluid dynamics/physics with simulation data, so Physics and Simulation experiment apply, and no biomedical domain term fits.

rationale: The study relies on Mendelian randomization, differential expression, single-cell RNA-seq, pseudo-temporal and cell-communication analyses, which are statistical/bioinformatics methods rather than named ML models, so no modelling fields apply. Domains reflect transcriptomic cancer genomics centered on esophageal cancer and an lncRNA immune regulator.

The paper trains five classical ML classifiers (SVM, RF, LR, bagged decision trees, GP) on radiomics features for supervised MCI detection, using LASSO among feature-reduction steps, while the deep VB-net segmentation network is applied as an existing pretrained tool. The subject is MR-imaging-based diagnosis of cognitive impairment, hence Medicine/Imaging/Neurology with Medical imaging and MRI at tier 3.

The paper develops and validates a PCA-based feature selection approach on resting-state fMRI connectivity data to identify robust functional connectivity biomarkers in psychiatric disorders (MDD, schizophrenia, ASD). PCA is the only named model, trained on the study's data without labels, so the learning paradigm is unsupervised; the supervised feature selection methods mentioned are only comparators.

The paper trains YOLOv5 variants and Faster R-CNN object detectors on annotated lower-extremity CT angiograms to classify stents, stenoses, and occlusions, which is supervised deep learning applied to medical imaging. The clinical decision-support context supports the Medical informatics tag alongside Imaging.

The study trains an orthogonal PLS-DA model and a decision tree on targeted plasma metabolomics data to discriminate AUD patients from controls, both supervised classical ML models trained in-house. The subject domain is biomedical (psychiatry/metabolomics biomarker discovery), with no deeper tier-3 vocabulary match.

The paper adapts a pretrained LLM (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) into an AI data-extraction model for oncology systematic reviews, refining it against human reference extractions (precision/recall/F1 evaluation), i.e. supervised adaptation of an LLM for NLP-based literature curation. Domains center on AI-assisted processing of biomedical literature rather than on the oncology content itself.

The paper applies the SuStaIn algorithm to post-mortem pathology and clinical data to infer disease subtypes and progression trajectories, an unsupervised subtype/progression model fitted on the study data; the digital pathology pipeline's machine learning is unnamed, so no further model types can be tagged. Domains centre on neurodegenerative disease (Lewy body dementia) with quantitative pathology and APOE genotype-to-phenotype analysis.

A retrospective clinical study trains a multivariable logistic regression model (presented as a nomogram) to predict meropenem-related thrombocytopenia in pulmonary infection patients, validating it with ROC, calibration, and decision curve analysis. The work sits in clinical pharmacology/drug-safety for a respiratory infection population.

Neuroimaging (T1 and resting-state fMRI) study of epilepsy classified under Medicine/Neurology/Imaging, with MRI-based modalities at tier 3. The abstract states four machine learning classifiers were trained to distinguish FBTCS+ from FBTCS- patients (supervised classification), but names no specific algorithm or architecture, so model_type and model_family are left empty.

model_type: ["skin color monitoring algorithm (SCMA)", "pulse wave monitoring algorithm (PWMA)"]
rationale: The paper develops and evaluates its own AI algorithms (SCMAs and PWMAs) on data from human participants, validated against expert assessments and pulse oximetry, implying supervised learning, but no specific architecture or model family is named in the abstract, so model_family stays empty per the evidence rules. The subject is postoperative flap monitoring in surgical care, with an informatics/monitoring-technology angle.

model_type: ["k-means", "hierarchical clustering", "spectral clustering", "Gaussian mixture model", "t-SNE", "random forest", "logistic regression"]

Domains reflect neonatal gut microbiome sequencing plus SCFA metabolite profiling.

The paper trains a random forest model with cross-validation on retrospective TKA navigation/CT data to predict cartilage wear corrections, a supervised classical ML ensemble task. The clinical subject is knee alignment assessment in arthroplasty using CT and imageless navigation, hence musculoskeletal medicine with medical imaging.

model_type: ["principal component analysis", "orthogonal partial least squares discriminant analysis"]
rationale: The paper is a metabolomics comparison of tea fixation workflows, profiling volatile and non-volatile metabolites by LC-MS/MS and GC-MS. PCA (unsupervised dimensionality reduction) and OPLS-DA (supervised discriminant modelling) are the only multivariate models applied; no other ML/AI method is named.

The abstract trains supervised classifiers on hospitalization data to predict pulmonary Long Covid sequelae but names no specific algorithm: a 'traditional shallow learner' (classical ML), an 'ensemble of classifiers' (ensemble learning), and multimodal models (multimodal learning). Hence model_type stays empty while the three explicitly named families are tagged.

The paper trains supervised models (LASSO for feature selection, GBDT and LightGBM for prediction) on its own cardiac arrest cohort to predict ROSC. Domain is cardiology/critical care medicine with a machine learning focus; no tier3 term applies.

The paper trains codonGPT, a generative mRNA language model, from scratch on 338k mRNA sequences (self-supervised language modeling) and then optimizes it with reinforcement learning under biological constraints. Domains center on computational biology / bioinformatics applied to mRNA (gene transcript) design, with machine learning as the enabling methodology.

The paper develops a 22-species qRT-PCR test and trains/tests an 'MDL-BV index' classifier for bacterial vaginosis diagnosis, i.e. a supervised classification model trained in this study. Since the abstract names no specific algorithm or model family for the diagnostic index, model_type and model_family are left empty per the evidence rules.

The study trains CSF1R-prediction classifiers on MRI radiomics and deep-learning features using 12 classic machine learning classifiers, with SVM, random forest and naive Bayes explicitly named and achieving the best metrics. Domain is oncology/neuroimaging (glioma MRI radiomics), and the deep-learning feature extractor plus named classical classifiers support the family tags.

The study applies an existing AI-guided quantitative CCTA software to derive plaque and stenosis variables in a multicenter prognostic cohort, with no training or fine-tuning described and no algorithm named, so the tool is tagged verbatim. Multivariable and Cox/AUC analyses are statistical association testing rather than the paper's predictive ML models, and the core clinical domains are cardiology and coronary CT imaging.

The study fine-tunes DistilBERT for supervised three-class classification of Reddit posts about living kidney donation and separately applies GPT-3.5 (ChatGPT) via systematic zero-shot prompt engineering, so both a fine-tuned and a prompted pretrained LLM are reported. Domains center on medical NLP applied to a nephrology-related health topic.

The study evaluates the pretrained AlphaFold 3 structure-prediction tool on aptamer targets without any further training, so model_use is applied as-is with no learning paradigm. Domains center on computational/bioinformatics nucleic acid structure prediction, and AlphaFold 3 is a deep-learning model applied verbatim as named.

The paper applies NLP (topic modeling and sentiment analysis) to scraped Twitter data to characterize parental attitudes toward children's COVID-19 vaccination; topic modeling corresponds to latent Dirichlet allocation, an unsupervised classical ML method trained on the study's own corpus, while no specific algorithm is named for sentiment analysis.

The paper sequences full-length 16S rRNA amplicons from calf fecal samples (microbiome/metagenomics domain) and trains Random Forest and SVM classifiers on Boruta-selected bacterial features to distinguish diarrheic from healthy calves; LEfSe and Boruta are excluded from model_type per the feature-selection/statistical-analysis rules.

The paper trains multiple machine learning and deep learning algorithms on 5478 MCC cases with 76 clinical variables to predict treatment recommendations, a supervised multi-target classification task, but names no specific algorithm or architecture, so model_type is left empty while the explicitly stated model families are tagged. Domain is clinical oncology decision support.

The paper integrates GEO datasets (WGCNA, differential expression, immune infiltration) to identify NSCLC diagnostic biomarkers, with a hybrid supervised machine learning feature-selection approach combining lasso regression and random forest. WGCNA and enrichment analyses are pipeline/network methods rather than trained ML models, so only lasso and random forest are tagged as model types.

The paper trains personalized lightweight CNNs for sEMG gesture classification, a supervised deep learning application in assistive biomedical engineering. No pretrained/foundation models are prompted or applied as-is; only the CNN family is named.

An observational cardiology study of Lp(a) and the CTI index versus angiographic coronary lesion burden; the abstract mentions internally validated machine-learning analyses with SHAP but names no algorithm, so model_type and model_family stay empty. The ML models predicting high Gensini score/multivessel disease were trained on the study's own data in a supervised manner.

The study trains radiomics ML classifiers and ResNet34-based 2D/2.5D/3D deep learning models on multicenter CT data, then fuses their outputs via an SVM-based stacking ensemble, all in a supervised paradigm. The domain is oncological imaging (prediction of tumor micronecrosis and progression in ccRCC).

The paper trains a WOA-optimized random forest (WOA-RF) on drilling geological data for mine water-inrush risk prediction, with PCA optimizing the entropy weighting and Kriging interpolation for spatial data enhancement. The whale optimization algorithm only tunes the RF and is therefore not listed as a separate model; the geology/mining subject falls outside the biomedical domain vocabularies, so only Environmental science applies as the closest tier-2 term.

The paper applies Google's pretrained MediaPipe Hands hand-tracking framework as-is to derive AR-based joint angle measurements, with no training or fine-tuning reported. Domain centers on hand surgery (musculoskeletal medicine) using camera-based computer vision, with reliability/validity statistics (ICC) not constituting a trained model.

Single-cell RNA-seq analysis of PBMCs in myasthenia gravis with WGCNA and unspecified integrative machine learning to identify hub gene PLEK; WGCNA is a network pipeline (not a model) and no algorithm is named, so model_type/model_family are empty while supervised training is implied by biomarker identification. WGCNA excluded, ML algorithm unnamed.

The paper trains ML classifiers on fMRI data to distinguish PTSD vs cognitive-impairment groups (supervised classification), but the abstract names no specific algorithm or architecture, so model_type and model_family stay empty. Structural equation modeling is a statistical analysis of associations, not a listed ML model, and the transcriptomic comparisons are correlation/enrichment analyses.

Mortality risk prediction models were trained on MIMIC-IV data with LASSO feature selection and eight ML algorithms, of which logistic regression performed best; this is supervised classical machine learning. SHAP is excluded as an explainability method, and the other seven algorithms are unnamed so cannot be tagged.

The paper trains a U-Net from scratch on 20 CT datasets to auto-contour parotid glands, a supervised deep-learning segmentation task in radiation oncology for head and neck cancer. Domains reflect the clinical oncology/imaging setting with medical imaging as the specific application area.

The chapter reports several newly trained deep learning tools for cryo-EM (CryoTransformer, CryoSegNet, CryoTEN, Cryo2Struct) built on transformer, U-Net/UNETR++ and attention-gated architectures, with an HMM used for chain assembly, plus pretrained components applied as-is (SAM, AlphaFold3) in the multimodal MICA framework. Models are trained on labelled cryo-EM data (supervised), so the domain spans structural biology and machine learning with protein structure analysis/prediction as core topics.

Deep learning models were trained on whole slide images to classify the molecular groups of lung neuroendocrine tumours, but the abstract names no specific architecture, so only the deep learning family is tagged. The multi-omic study (WGS, transcriptomics, methylation) with supervised deep learning classification supports the oncology/genomics domains and related tier-3 terms.

This is a survey study of dermatologists' acceptance of digital health interventions; exploratory factor analysis reduces the Likert items, which then feed a 2-step cluster analysis, all unsupervised methods fitted on the paper's own survey data. No AI model is trained or applied by the authors themselves (AI/teledermatology is only the survey topic).

The paper trains a customized decision tree (with a novel min_groups_leaf parameter) on Alzheimer's brain proteomics data for supervised feature selection across five proteomic data sets. The subject is proteomics data analysis, with machine learning as the methodological core; no other model types are named.

The paper develops and validates a proprietary AI algorithm that estimates uroflow parameters from smartphone voiding videos, implying supervised training for a continuous flow-rate regression task, but the abstract names no specific algorithm or architecture, so model_type and model_family are left empty. The subject is urological diagnostics (LUTS/uroflowmetry) with a video-based AI measurement component.

The paper trains simple interpretable models on CPT-II behavioral features to classify ADHD-likely vs control-likely participants, with a decision tree explicitly named to produce explanation rules; this is supervised classical machine learning applied to psychiatric (ADHD) research. No deep, generative, or other model families are named in the abstract.

The paper presents an end-to-end AR task-guidance system using AI models for perceptual grounding, attention, and reasoning, but names no specific algorithms, architectures, or training procedures. No biomedical domain applies; the work is a computer science system-design contribution, with no model reported as trained or fine-tuned in the study.

The paper trains seven supervised classifiers (XGBoost, LightGBM, SVM, etc.) on NHANES biomarker/exposure data for CVD risk prediction, with LASSO used for feature selection; SHAP and transcriptomic time-course analyses are interpretation/validation, not model types. Domains center on cardiovascular medicine with explainable ML, supported by transcriptomic validation.

The paper trains ARIMA, LSTM, and an attention-enhanced LSTM (ATLSTM) on geotechnical inclinometer time series to predict retaining-wall deformation, a supervised forecasting task. The subject is geotechnical/civil engineering, which falls outside the biomedical domain vocabularies, so no domain terms apply.

The paper trains XGBoost, logistic regression, and MLP models (single-task, multi-class, and multi-task variants) on electronic healthcare records to predict in-hospital mortality and length of stay, a supervised learning task in clinical/medical informatics. No pretrained, prompted, or generative models are involved, and no specific subdomain tier3 terms are central beyond routine hospital EHR data use.

Six supervised ML algorithms were trained on the PMA 2019 survey data to predict modern contraceptive use, with XGBoost, logistic regression and support vector machines explicitly named and compared; information gain was feature selection and 'dimensionality reduction' preprocessing, not a named model. The domain is reproductive-health/public-health survey analysis rather than omics or bioinformatics.

The abstract compares generic supervised models against clustering on registry data without naming any specific algorithm or architecture, so model_type and model_family stay empty. Both a supervised step (outcome prediction) and an unsupervised step (clustering) are performed in the study, so both paradigms are tagged.

The study compares gut fungal communities in ACVD patients vs controls via shotgun metagenomics with network analysis, and builds disease-prediction models from bacterial and fungal taxa. Since the abstract names no specific algorithm or model family for the predictive models, only the supervised training use is tagged, and model_type/model_family remain empty.

The paper trains a Random Forest regression model on email content indicators to predict sensitivity scores, with SHAP used only for explainability (excluded). Rule-based analysis, AES-ECC encryption, and the Enron dataset are pipeline components, not additional ML models.

rationale: The study externally validates existing three-predictor prognostic scoring models (Anzuategui, Tomita, Modified Bauer, Van der Linden, Sioutos) in spinal metastasis surgery patients without training any new model; the abstract names no machine-learning algorithm, so model_type lists the applied prediction tools verbatim and model_family stays empty per the evidence rules.

The paper trains lasso-based feature selection, isolation forest outlier handling, and random forest (best of five evaluated) classifiers on metabolomic data to predict recurrent acute pancreatitis, all supervised classical ML with an ensemble component; the clinical subject is disease-risk prediction from metabolomic biomarkers.

The paper trains convolutional models for network anomaly detection under federated learning (FedAvg and FedProx) on the NSL-KDD dataset with differential privacy, a supervised task on centralized and distributed clients. It is a pure computer science/cybersecurity study, so only the machine learning and data security domain terms apply.

The paper trains an alternating decision tree (ADTree) on immunohistochemical marker data to predict chemotherapy response, a supervised classification task; ADTree is a boosting-based ensemble of decision trees. The domain is oncology/biomarker research in breast cancer with no additional tier-3 terms needed.

The CCADDAS pipeline applies PARC clustering and UMAP (unsupervised) plus an anomaly-detection aberrancy scale, and trains a deep neural network on expert-defined normal subsets (supervised) for automated gating. The paper is a hematology/cytometry application (CLL MRD detection by flow cytometry); no tier-3 term fits centrally.

The paper trains an offline reinforcement learning model on SRTR waitlist trajectories to optimize wait/delist/transplant decisions, so model_use is 'trained in this study' with the reinforcement paradigm. No concrete algorithm or architecture is named, so the model type is tagged verbatim as 'offline reinforcement learning' with no applicable family; the domain is clinical transplant decision-making supported by ML.

The paper trains DeepRespNet, a supervised deep regression model combining a transformer-style encoder (spatiotemporal convolution + multi-head self-attention) with a BiLSTM, on video-derived rPPG and motion signals; the joint use of two data modalities makes it multimodal learning. The domain is physiological measurement/remote healthcare monitoring, hence Medicine/Physiology with no specific tier3 method fitting.

The paper describes a national health-record registry with AI tools (custom OCR, concept-based search, AI-based de-identification) developed or adapted in-house, but no specific algorithm, architecture, or pretrained product is named. Since only generic 'AI' is mentioned without naming any model type or family, model_type and model_family are left empty; the tools are developed/refined within the project, hence 'trained in this study' with paradigm unstated.

The paper develops iterative adaptive dynamic programming (approximate dynamic programming/reinforcement learning) for finite-horizon optimal control, training neural networks to approximate the performance index, the control policy, and the system model, so the paradigm is reinforcement learning with (in 2011, non-deep) neural networks as the learning model. The subject is optimal control theory, best captured by Mathematics > Applied mathematics, with no deeper EDAM topic term applicable.

domain_tier3: ["Protein folding, stability and design", "Structure prediction", "Molecular modelling"]
rationale: The paper develops PrefixProt, which learns virtual prefix tokens as control tags on a pretrained protein language model via prefix-tuning (parameter-efficient adaptation) to steer de novo protein generation toward target structural and functional properties. The pretrained ProtLM is fine-tuned/adapted on labelled property data, making the training supervised, and the generative ProtLM architecture places it in the deep learning / large language model / generative AI families.

MI-DDI trains an MPNN on molecular graphs and transformer encoders on drug SMILES in a supervised manner to predict drug-drug interactions, both being deep learning architectures. The domain is computational DDI prediction from molecular structures, best captured by computational biology with cheminformatics and pharmacology focus.

The paper trains PCA, unsupervised clustering, and stepwise LDA on its own obesity cohort, combining an unsupervised clustering step with a supervised classification step (LDA on the test set). Domain is medicine applied via data-driven phenotyping in a medical informatics venue; no tier-3 term fits sarcopenic obesity phenotyping.

The paper trains a heterogeneous graph neural network (StrokeTHG) on EHR data for multi-horizon stroke mortality prediction, alongside tabular baselines it fits itself (logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost). The domain is clinical predictive modeling of stroke outcomes, best captured as Medicine with Medical informatics and Neurology.

SELDI serum proteomic spectra were used to train a decision classification tree (Biomarker Patterns) to distinguish lung cancer from healthy controls, i.e. supervised training of a classical ML model on labelled patient samples. The subject is proteomic biomarker discovery for oncology, so Omics/Proteomics/Oncology with Protein expression best capture the domain.

The paper trains four models (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, neural networks) on kMC-simulated microstructure descriptors to predict grain morphology from process parameters, i.e. supervised regression. SHAP is an explainability method and is excluded; the domain is materials/process simulation (physics), outside the biomedical vocabularies, so tier2/tier3 remain empty.

The paper trains ensemble deep-learning models on deep-sequencing data of a mutational RBD library to predict antibody binding and escape, a supervised learning task; the abstract names no specific architecture, so model_type is left empty. Domains reflect antibody therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2 with an ML methodology core.

The paper builds a normalization scheme plus a correlation-based intra-segment classification criterion to discriminate abnormal from normal LV wall motion, which is a supervised classification task fitted on the study's own cardiac MR data, but no specific algorithm or model family is named in the abstract.

The paper trains a random forest classifier on sequence-derived features to predict ion channel families and subfamilies, with mRMR used for feature selection (a task, not a model type). Domain is computational biology/bioinformatics applied to protein sequence classification.

The paper develops an unsupervised active learning framework trained from scratch, combining dominant-set and spectral graph-theoretic clustering in a hierarchy. The SVM-based supervised active learning is only a benchmark comparator and is therefore not tagged.

The paper develops and trains HAMRL variants of multiagent reinforcement learning algorithms (Minimax-Q, Q-learning family) evaluated in adversarial domains. Reinforcement is the sole learning paradigm; no model_family term in the vocabulary fits Q-learning beyond its reinforcement paradigm designation.

The paper develops an unsupervised hybrid PCA + spatial fuzzy c-means (with Gaussian kernel) segmentation pipeline for cDNA microarray images, so the model types are PCA and fuzzy c-means trained on the authors' own image data. Domain tags reflect microarray-based gene expression analysis handled through bioinformatics/image processing.

The paper develops and trains a piecewise linear network with an orthonormal least squares procedure for regression-based feature selection, a supervised task with no specific biomedical application, so the domain is machine learning within computer science. Floating search is a feature-selection strategy rather than a trained model, so it is not listed as a model type.

The paper trains its own multiview representation learning method optimized via information-theoretic objectives (intraview coding rate reduction using class structure, and interview mutual information), placing it in representation learning with a supervised class-organizing component and a self-supervised cross-view consistency component. No biomedical application is described, so only the computer science / machine learning domains apply.

model_type: ["gradient boosting", "Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial model", "Hurdle Negative Binomial model"]
rationale: The paper trains gradient boosting machines and fits parametric count models (ZINB, HNB) within simulation studies and a real-data propensity score analysis, a supervised causal-inference setting. The domain is statistical methodology for observational study design, not a biomedical application, so no tier3 term applies.

domain_tier3: ["Protein structure analysis", "Structure prediction", "Protein folding, stability and design"]
rationale: SPIN trains a neural network on fragment-derived sequence profiles and structure-derived energy profiles to predict sequence profiles from protein structures, a supervised prediction task. No pretrained or prompted model is used, and the 2014-era neural network is a plain (non-deep) architecture, so it maps to 'classic neural network'.

The paper trains hybrid RNN and LSTM models (with metaheuristic optimizers used only to tune them) on hydrological data to forecast dam inflows and groundwater levels, i.e. supervised deep learning applied to environmental/water-resource management. Climate models (MRI-ESM2 etc.) are physical simulation tools, not ML models, so they are not tagged.

The paper develops a nearest-neighbor-based data reliability measure that generates OWA aggregation weights from the data itself, without labels, and applies it to alias detection and unsupervised feature selection. The k-nearest-neighbor reliability assessment is trained/fitted on the data in an unsupervised manner; OWA operators are aggregation operators tagged verbatim.

model_type: ["Segment Anything Model (SAM 1)", "Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2)", "automatic mask generator"]
rationale: The paper applies pretrained Segment Anything Models zero-shot (with only AMG hyperparameter tuning, no weight updates) inside an annotation tool for agricultural image segmentation, so no learning paradigm applies. Domains centre on computer-vision tooling for agriculture: computer science with agricultural science and imaging, plus dataset annotation.

The paper develops a dictionary/token-based protein name recognition system whose parameters are optimized with machine learning, but no specific ML algorithm or architecture is named in the abstract, so model_type and model_family remain empty. It is a text-mining/NLP application in computational biology, with parameter fitting implying supervised training of the method in this study.

The paper develops MR-AIV, a physics-informed architecture that fits 3D velocity, pressure and permeability fields to DCE-MRI data with physics-based constraints, so the model is trained in this study with physics-constrained (label-free) optimization. Domains center on brain MRI imaging applied to neurology-related fluid dynamics.

The paper's subject is epilepsy patient information needs, analysed with an unsupervised topic-modelling approach applied to social-media text, so Medicine/Neurology with NLP as an applied method. The abstract names no specific topic-modelling algorithm (e.g. LDA), so model_type is left empty while the unsupervised training paradigm is retained.

The paper trains ensembles of diverse machine learning algorithms on SNP/phenotype data to build multi-marker association tests (supervised phenotype prediction), but names no specific algorithm, so only the ensemble learning family is taggable. The subject is GWAS-based genetic association analysis of asthma cohorts.

model_type: ["linear discriminant analysis", "partial least squares", "principal component regression", "principal component analysis", "independent component analysis", "support vector machine", "ensemble methods", "linear regression"]
rationale: The paper trains multiple classifiers (LDA, PLS, PCR, SVM, ensemble methods, regularized linear regression) on labelled MRS spectra, with unsupervised feature extraction (PCA, ICA, wavelets) feeding the supervised models. Domain is biomedical (brain tumor MR spectroscopy diagnosis), hence Machine learning + Oncology and imaging-related tier3 terms.

The paper trains a sphere-shaped (one-class) support vector machine to enclose encephalic tissue data in kernel space for 3D MRI modeling, fitting models on the paper's own image data without labelled classes. The Immune Algorithm is used only to tune the SVM's parameters, so it is not listed as a separate model type.

The paper develops a low-rank matrix decomposition method with a structural incoherence constraint, learning basis matrices from face image data (unsupervised decomposition) followed by class-based recognition (supervised classification). Eigenfaces and sparse representation-based classification are prior/comparator methods, not the paper's own models.

The paper develops the ICE computational method, which iteratively learns bias-correction weights from Hi-C contact matrices (an unsupervised, data-driven fitting) and then applies eigenvector decomposition, a PCA-like dimensionality-reduction technique, to the corrected maps. Domains reflect the genome-wide 3C/Hi-C chromosome-organization subject matter.

model_type: ["random forest", "bagging", "support vector machine", "generalized additive model", "linear regression", "nonlinear regression"]
rationale: The paper fits parametric linear/nonlinear regression models and recalibrates SAFER coefficients, and evaluates them against RF, bagged trees, SVM and GAM trained on Landsat-8-derived features, so all models are trained in-study under supervised learning. The subject (evapotranspiration estimation for water management) is environmental/agricultural, best captured by tier2 terms since no earth-science tier1 exists; the tier3 list offers no relevant term.

The study applies scRNA-seq analysis (Seurat for unsupervised clustering and dimensionality reduction) as-is, alongside non-ML analyses (Mendelian randomization, GSVA, molecular docking) that are excluded from model_type. No model is trained or fine-tuned in this paper, and no specific ML algorithm is named beyond clustering and dimensionality reduction.

The paper develops and trains LDA/QR, a supervised two-stage linear discriminant analysis for dimensionality reduction on face and text data, with QR decomposition replacing the PCA stage of the classical PCA+LDA pipeline. It is a computer-science/applied-mathematics pattern-recognition contribution evaluated on classification benchmarks.
